## Tidepool Landing Page — Build Plan

**Global system:** Carry over the reference's deep forest green + coral palette, but shift backgrounds to warm cream so screenshots breathe. Keep the vertical week-timeline rail pinned to the left edge — Mon–Fri nodes glow coral as each section scrolls into view, mapping page sections to days. Display type: warm serif for headlines; clean sans for body.

**1. Hero (Monday node lit).** Two columns: left, one long, flowing sentence headline in the reference's chatty style — *"Put your whole team around one shared plan that shows who's doing what by when, absorbs changes the moment they happen, and ends the Monday meeting where nobody remembers what they promised."* Coral CTA beneath: "Start your week." Right: Tidepool board screenshot in a soft-cornered frame, with a hand-drawn coral arrow curving from headline to UI, annotated *"your week, live"* in handwritten script.

**2. Trust strip.** Thin cream band, six small-team logos in muted green, no claims.

**3. Feature rows (Tue–Thu nodes).** Three alternating image-left/text-right rows, each tied to a timeline node: shared weekly board, async check-ins, Friday wrap-up recap. Copy is verb-led and concrete ("Drag it to Wednesday. Everyone sees it."). Cropped, real-looking UI shots — no stock illustration.

**4. Pull quote.** Full-bleed forest-green band. Quote set in monospace, cream text, centered: *"We stopped asking 'who has this?' — the week just shows us."* Attribution in small-caps sans: a team lead at a ten-person startup.

**5. Getting started (light band).** Three horizontal steps — invite your team, sketch the week, let it update itself. Numbered in coral circles echoing the node style.

**6. Final CTA (Friday node lit).** Centered headline ("Plan Friday's retro on Monday"), coral button, one-line reassurance: free for teams of five.

**7. Footer.** Cream, four link columns, small repeating wave-line motif along the bottom edge.
final:
**Key upgrades:** the headline now closes on a concrete image (the reference's "milk" move); the rail becomes an animated narrative device instead of a passive indicator; the hand-drawn annotation recurs as a motif; a new section handles the real competitor — the spreadsheet/group chat.

**Global system.** Keep cream backgrounds, forest green + coral, serif display / sans body. Upgrade the rail: fixed left, Mon–Sun nodes; a coral "now" dot travels down it like a calendar's current-time line; nodes illuminate as their section arrives; hovering a node shows a handwritten section label. Weekend nodes stay hollow, tagged *"off."* Mobile: rail collapses to a top progress bar.

**1. Hero (Monday).** Headline: *"Put your whole team around one living plan that shows who's doing what by when, updates the instant reality changes, and quietly reshuffles everything else so the week holds together — even when Wednesday goes sideways."* Coral CTA "Start your week." Screenshot right; the hand-drawn coral arrow draws itself on scroll, annotated *"your week, live."*

**2. Trust strip.** Logos strung along a thin rail-like line with tiny nodes; one stat: *"1,900 small teams plan their Monday here."*

**3. Feature rows (Tue–Thu).** Three alternating rows, one per node, each screenshot carrying a single hand-drawn annotation. Tue: "Drag it to Wednesday. Everyone sees it" (arrow: *"moved → everyone knows"*). Wed: "Check-ins without the meeting." Thu: "Reality, absorbed" — blocked tasks auto-slide to the next open slot, proving the headline's "reshuffles" claim.

**4. Pull quote.** Full-bleed green band, cream monospace: *"Our Monday sync went from an hour to a five-minute scroll."* Small-caps attribution: ops lead, 12-person team.

**5. Objection band (new).** *"Your spreadsheet had a good run."* Split visual: chaotic group-chat thread vs. one calm board. Warm, not smug.

**6. Getting started.** Three coral-numbered steps: invite your team, sketch the week, let it keep itself current.

**7. Final CTA (Friday).** *"Plan Friday's retro on Monday."* Coral button, "Free up to five people."

**8. Footer.** Cream, four columns, wave-line motif — the tidepool, literalized.
